svg.title: DIBBS Parts Broker Architecture
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-dibbs-broker-architecture; chapter number: 11; title: DIBBS Parts Broker Architecture; subtitle: One narrow FSC lane, quoted every day; caption: DVN reports DLA posts 2,000 to 3,000 solicitations a day, and the active DIBBS vendor pool shrank to about 8,500 from roughly 15,000 before the pandemic. Roughly 99% of awards go to the cheapest bid.; assumptions note: Spokes are functions, not hires, and may all sit with one owner-operator. No headcount was testified. Tooling ranges from FedOpp browser-built batch files to DVN's DLA BUS catalog uploads and Gov Scraper at $100 a month.; note: Sources - Tris10 @ MeND (v4ulUMKE5xA, JE_OOJ3NAVk), Secureframe with Tristan Thomas (v7nJCLRc0uo), The DLA Vendor Network (DVN) with Ki Hendris (jjX9klCZFKI, MyfmHjDF9HI), Loocey DLA & GovCon (LzmJyrGyMBw), FedOpp (bTs2wy13K1c).; chart type: org_architecture; center: role: DIBBS Broker; headcount: Owner-operator in a 3 to 5 FSC lane; focus: Quote every day, because bid count tracks award count (Tris10 @ MeND); spokes: role: RFQ Screener; type: Solicitation intake; kpi: Read the full solicitation, filter Approved Sources is null, and reject parts from non-qualifying countries such as China or Afghanistan; role: Supplier Sourcer; type: Supply side; kpi: Map every NSN to the manufacturer part number with nsn-now, then call instead of email; role: Pricer; type: Margin control; kpi: 10-15% margin anchored to procurement history, since asking 20-30% gets underbid (Tristan Thomas); role: Invoicing and Cash; type: Collections; kpi: Net 30 terms with the government paying in 23 to 25 days on average, and My Invoice checked every Friday
